findings.message:
NEW, and it is the same defect class run 003 named, displaced rather than removed. The repaired
misconception box now misrepresents the very source it rests on.

docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-04/topic-04.mdx:110-112 reads:
  "**A misconception this corrects:** *appraisal and professional development are the same
   process.* They are related and must be connected, and holding both in a single instrument is
   hard enough that **most systems separate them in practice**."

The absolute clause run 003 flagged ("cannot be the same instrument") is gone, and the box no
longer collides with the RRQ-04 mark scheme. But the clause that replaced it is an empirical
generalisation about international practice, it is unsourced, and the bound excerpt for this
exact point states the opposite. specs/content/efmp-302/sources/texts/isore2009.md, para 17,
verbatim: "In practice, countries rarely use a pure form of teacher evaluation model but rather
a unique combination that integrates multiple purposes and methodologies (Stronge and Tucker,
2003)." A "pure form" is a purely formative or purely summative model; Isore's finding is that
systems typically COMBINE the purposes, which is the negation of "most systems separate them in
practice".

It also contradicts the same file fifteen lines earlier, which paraphrases the source correctly:
  topic-04.mdx:95-97 "She reports that countries rarely use a pure form of either, that a single
  framework \"can serve both summative and formative purposes\", and she devotes an annex section
  to *conciliating the summative and formative purposes in a comprehensive approach*."
and topic-01.mdx:145-146 "systems that hold both exist, and they do it by deciding the trade-off
openly instead of leaving it to chance."

So the structure run 003 objected to survives: a box whose format tells the learner it is the
corrected truth carries a claim the body of the same topic, and the cited source, both deny.
The consequence is milder than run 003's - no candidate is now denied a mark by RRQ-04 - which is
why this is recorded as a fresh blocking finding rather than the old one reopened.

REPAIR (one clause, and it is the only site: a corpus grep for "most systems" over the unit
returns topic-04.mdx:112 alone): state the difficulty without the invented frequency claim, e.g.
"...and holding both in a single instrument is hard enough that the two have to be kept
deliberately distinct inside it". Do not substitute another frequency claim; the bound source
supports a statement about difficulty and about deliberate reconciliation, not a count of
systems. Do not weaken :95-97 to match :112 instead.

VERDICT ON RUN-003 [1] (the accreditation claim, seven sites): RESOLVED. The softened wording is
within what the declaration supports, and the open question is honestly recorded rather than
quietly closed.
All seven sites are repaired, checked individually:
  topic-01.mdx:105-106 "they are the framework this country's teacher education is built to"
  topic-01.mdx:127     "This is why your own degree is designed around it."
  topic-01.mdx:196-197 "is the reference this country's teacher education is built to"
  topic-02.mdx:43-45   "the framework against which teacher education programmes in Pakistan are
                        designed, which is why they shape your own degree as well as your later
                        practice"
  topic-02.mdx:178-179 "are the framework this country's teacher education is built to"
  topic-04.mdx:48      "Your B.Ed, built to the National Professional Standards, is the mechanism

A corpus grep for "accredit" over docs/semester-1/efmp-302/unit-04/ now returns exactly one hit,
index.mdx:51, and that one is a prerequisite pointer to Unit 1's content ("Unit 1 supplies
professionalism, accreditation and professional bodies"), not a claim about what the NPST
accredits. No figure label, alt text or manifest row carries the claim.
Why this now passes where "accredited against" failed. Accreditation is a specific regulatory act
with a named actor, and asserting it told the learner something about the legal status of their
own degree that npst-pakistan-2009's declaration does not cover and that the NACTE finding in
specs/gaps.md:81-90 positively contradicts. "Built to" / "designed around" / "shape" assert design
influence, not regulatory status, and they no longer collide with the NACTE evidence: a programme
can be designed with reference to the national standards while being accredited by NACTE against
NACTE's own standards. Both propositions can hold at once, which is what the previous wording
denied. The claim is also corroborated inside the bundle rather than resting on the unretrievable
key alone: the approved course guide makes NPST a named unit topic (1st 2026.txt:873 "4.2 Overview
of the National Professional Standards for Teachers in Pakistan") and lists it as a recommended
reference (:656), and the HEC/USAID 2025 course guides teach it as course content
(TestDevEval_Sept13.txt:1641-1648).
The declaration was NOT stretched to cover this. specs/content/efmp-302/sources/unit-04.md:40 is
byte-unchanged in what it discloses - the ten standard names, the three-part division and the 2009
MoE/UNESCO/USAID origin - which is the route run 003 explicitly warned against taking.
And the underlying question is not closed by the repair: specs/gaps.md:105 records the Unit 4
instance against the existing open Unit 2 escalation, names what changed and why, states that the
declaration supports the new wording, and ends "The underlying question is unchanged and still
needs the decision described above", pointing at gaps.md:90 ("the curriculum owner or a reviewer
with access"). That is an honest and complete record. The escalation remains open in the
repository; it is not carried as an unresolved finding of this report because the prose no longer
overstates it.
